newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares in negative territory at bourse open.
newsitem.headline: German shares in negative territory at bourse open.

text.p: German share traders were expecting a quiet day's trade on Monday, with trading sentiment hit by lower German bonds, a still-weak dollar and an unhelpfully low close on Wall Street on Friday.
In early bourse trade the DAX index, which measures floor trade in 30 blue-chip German shares, was down 3.27 points at 2,551.89 points.

"There is very little going on here today and volumes seem very thin. Also London is closed because of the bank holiday," said a Frankfurt dealer, adding that interest should pick up after the holiday season ends around next week.
Among shares on the move in early bourse trade was the specialty chemical SKW Trostberg AG, which went up more than four percent at 39.70 marks.

The increase was attributed to an announcement that SKW was buying Master Builders Technology (MBT), a subsidiary of the Swiss chemical group Sandoz and the SKW would not increase its capital to finance the deal.
"The purchase of MBT will be positively viewed. The price should be fair," said one trader.
Chemical shares were lower in pre-bourse trade on Monday after performing strongly on Friday, but they picked up again in bourse trade.
BASF AG was up 30 pfennigs at 43.90 marks, while Hoechst AG was up five pfennigs at 51.40 marks and Degussa AG was up 2.50 marks at 509.50.
